_about: Legend: The Boy Who Cried Wolf (Aesop, Greece). Jonny 27 Nov 21:10 Berlin picked H1 (teeth rule) + E1 (kid drives the flock into the square). Niche-findings build: wolf eyes frame 0, kid = hero of one night, one history line (L13) after the wolf's first move. Speakers N narrator, G grandmother, K kid, V village man. CAPTION TRIAL (his OK 21:10): big, low-middle, 2-4 words, key words red (wolf, teeth, see, eyes, voice); TikTok export without subtitles.

G.style: an old woman in her eighties, warm but stern, low slightly raspy voice, slow and calm

K.style: a twelve-year-old boy from a film, natural child actor, clearly a boy, voice not broken yet, curious and cheeky, speaks clearly with crisp diction

V.style: a gruff village man in his forties, out of breath, loud, no accent imitation

lines: Shout wolf only when you SEE its teeth.
urgent low whisper, off screen, over the wolf's eyes in the dark; the howl SFX + the hill carry 'sense + place' (Sol 27 Nov: the long version was too wordy for 3 s)
And if I already shouted twice?
Nine o'clock that night. The boy was bored. By two, he'd wish he'd kept his mouth shut.
quick storyteller, a smile in the voice, last sentence darker (RE-HOOK 1 at ~5 s)
shouting, fake panic, trying not to laugh
The whole village ran up the hill with sticks.
angry, out of breath, a village man
Nobody looked at the olive trees. Something in there was watching. And counting.
low, slow, a chill (RE-HOOK 2: the wolf's eyes are visible in the trees behind the villagers, the viewer sees what they don't)
Eleven o'clock. He did it again.
Fewer came. Angrier. His grandmother came last.
Twice now. You've used up your voice.
Two in the morning. Something howled in the olive trees.
The Greeks told this story two and a half thousand years ago. It always ends the same way. But this boy was about to try something new.
mysterious, last sentence quicker (RE-HOOK 3 at ~30 s, teases the twist)
WOLF! For real this time! WOLF!
Down in the village, the lights went out. One... by one.
Nobody came. And now there were more eyes.
Only when they SEE its teeth...
They won't believe my voice. So they'll have to see it.
And drove every sheep he had straight down into the village.
The flock came bleating through the square... and the wolf came right behind them.
This time, everyone saw the teeth.
Now I'm the boy who brought a wolf to town.
